EFFECT: “each time a model in your unit is destroyed by a melee attack, if that model has not fought this phase, roll one D6: on a 4+ … it can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks”. The def changes two things. (1) “before it has fought” drops “this phase”, so it reads as a model that has never fought. (2) “fights after” turns GW’s “can fight” into something it must do. The fix keeps the text’s condition and its “can”.

fix.def: Fight phase, just after an enemy unit selects it as a target: until the end of the phase, each time a model is destroyed by a melee attack, if that model has not fought this phase, on a D6 of 4+ it is not removed; it can fight after the attacking unit has finished its attacks, then is removed

why: Same two slips as the def. “before it has fought” drops GW’s “if that model has not fought this phase”, and “fights after” turns GW’s “it can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks” into a must. The rest is faithful: WHEN, TARGET “selected as the target of one or more of the attacking unit’s attacks”, 4+, removed afterwards.

fix.gist: Fight phase, just after an enemy unit selects its targets, your LEGIONES DAEMONICA KHORNE unit it targeted: until the end of the phase, each time a model in it is destroyed by a melee attack, if that model has not fought this phase, on a D6 of 4+ it is not removed; it can fight after the attacking unit has finished its attacks, then is removed.

The {movement:"either"} comes from derive.js’s Fire Overwatch modifier, which it applies to “always-on” ranged effects. Shudderblink is not always on. It is triggered “When a friendly … unit is selected to make an advance move”, and its [ASSAULT] lasts “until the end of the turn”, which is the unit’s own turn (advance moves are your Movement phase, 09.06). By the opponent’s Movement phase, where Fire Overwatch is used, the [ASSAULT] has ended. The approved Thulia Ghuld rows differ: their effect lasts “until the start of your next Command phase”. So there is no opponent’s-turn entry, and all phases are your turn: remove turns.

The only change extends the --expand-only “own” branch (opts.keep has 'own'; own stays in HIDE, so the app’s load is unchanged) from stats to ranged and melee rows. A weapon row’s from-keys are fields (A, S, D …) or weapon-ability names (“SUSTAINED HITS 1”), and the `f in ds` guard skips the ability names. The array-valued kw is never a from-key, so the !== comparison only compares strings. Run with keep:['own'], it gives own only where a rule changed a value (Relentless Rage A, Bane-Forged S, Daemonic Allegiance S …). Every resolved list except the new one is identical to main 24f66fe’s (loadData, JSON-equal), and no ARMIES entry of an existing list changed in the diff.

GW’s Blood Legion page (Faction Pack 1.2 p.123, “DETACHMENT RULE”) and Wahapedia both print two parts: MURDERCALL and BLOOD TAINTED. data.js has only Murdercall. from-json.js’s wahaDetachment() stops reading the rule segment at Murdercall’s “Errata” spoiler (note=true), so the Blood Tainted heading and its text after the spoiler are silently dropped, and texts.js did not catch it. Blood Tainted must be added with GW’s words, and the rule’s labels must be re-derived (it acts “At the end of a phase”: every phase, either turn). from-json.js should end a note at the next rule heading.
